A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeLL framework. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. V1 includes Appendices A–C; v3 integrates Appendix A into the main text and omits the other two analyses.

before.justification: V1 reports original CARLA experiments, including sequential learning, full-data evaluation, component ablations and reverse-order learning results.

after.justification: V3 retains original CARLA results for sequential learning, full-data evaluation, lifelong-learning baselines and component ablations.

M1.justification: The perception backbone, DPMM knowledge spaces, FFEM/TFEM attention and gating, evolutionary decoder, losses and training procedure remain unchanged. Wording revisions do not establish an algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: Both versions use Bench2Drive's same five driving competencies and DEV10 qualitative scenarios in CARLA. Removing the reverse training order changes evaluation procedure, not the represented data or task requirements.

E2.justification: Comparator sets remain unchanged in the corresponding retained experiments. The ER and PackNet comparison moves from v1 Appendix A/Table 4 to v3 Section 4.3/Table 2; the full-data comparison retains the same methods.

E3.justification: V3 drops the supplementary reverse-order evaluation and full-data ablation controls while retaining the main training settings, frame counts and budgets. Equation (12) corrects the printed forward-transfer summation from j=1+1 to j=i+1; unchanged retained scores do not establish that evaluation was rerun.

E4.justification: V1 Appendix B/Table 5 tests sensitivity to reversing the task sequence, and Appendix C/Table 6 tests component contributions under full-data learning. Both analyses disappear from v3, substantially narrowing robustness and ablation evidence. The lifelong-learning ablations and qualitative analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The reporting practice remains point estimates.

E6.justification: The entire reverse-order and full-data ablation result sets are removed. These include reverse-order FT of 32.28 for DeLL versus 35.00 for TF++, and full-data SR of 71.36 without the evolutionary decoder versus 68.63 for the full model. Numerical results in all retained tables are unchanged, including the relocated ER/PackNet comparison.

T1.justification: Equation (12) corrects the forward-transfer definition by summing over subsequent tasks starting at j=i+1. Section 3.3 also drops 'all' from the condition that the mediator intercepts directed input-to-output paths, making that condition less explicit. The remaining mathematical formulation is unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about dynamic knowledge spaces, causal enhancement, parallel decoding, the lifelong-learning protocol and superior performance. Reduced emphatic wording does not substantively redefine these claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of forgetting, knowledge transfer, component effects and cluster overlap remain substantively unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning alternating-optimization overhead and the CARLA-to-real-world domain gap; softened causal wording adds no explicit applicability qualification.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 retains the same training stages, epochs, learning rates, backbone freezing, optimizer resets, four L40 GPUs, batch size, training time and inference resource figures. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The same 57 works remain referenced, with unchanged substantive research positioning. Several preprint entries receive publication metadata and citation formatting updates. The first-work claim accompanying the ER/PackNet comparison is relocated from Appendix A.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, incorporates Appendix A into Section 4.3, removes the remaining supplementary sections, and adds acknowledgements. The main section hierarchy and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V1 Table 4 becomes v3 Table 2, subsequent tables are renumbered, and v1 Tables 5–6 disappear. Figures 3–4 and surrounding text are repositioned. All four figures retain the same content, and retained tables preserve their display structure.

improvement.justification: V3 usefully corrects Equation (12) and brings the existing ER/PackNet comparison into the main text. However, removing v1 Tables 5–6 reduces evidence on task-order sensitivity and component effectiveness, including mixed outcomes relevant to the retained broad claims. These losses outweigh the limited editorial gains, while the unchanged main method and results limit the overall deterioration.
